q: A pioneer of high-tech architecture who prized transparency and flexibility, this British architect co-designed the Centre Pompidou and later gave London its Lloyd's Building. Name him.
n: A British architect and a pioneer of the high-tech architecture movement, emphasizing transparency and flexibility in design. He co-designed the Centre Pompidou and contributed to numerous urban projects. Notable works: the Lloyd's Building (London) and the Millennium Dome (now The O2, London).

q: An architect's portfolio includes Karlsplatz Stadtbahn Station, Vienna; Vienna Postal Savings Bank; and Church of St. Leopold, Steinhof. Who designed these?
n: Otto Wagner's notable works are the Karlsplatz Stadtbahn Station in Vienna, exemplifying the transition from historicism to modernism, the Vienna Postal Savings Bank, and the Church of St. Leopold, Steinhof, a masterpiece of sacred architecture.

q: How would Joseph Paxton's architectural style best be classified?
n: Joseph Paxton's architectural style is Victorian / Prefabricated Iron-and-Glass Architecture. Joseph Paxton pioneered prefabricated iron-and-glass construction, exemplified by the Crystal Palace.

q: Norman Foster is most closely associated with which architectural style?
n: Norman Foster's architectural style is High-tech Architecture. Norman Foster is renowned for sleek, high-tech, sustainable architecture.

q: Chrysler Building, New York — these are among the notable works of which architect?
n: William Van Alen's notable work is the Chrysler Building, New York — an iconic skyscraper with a distinctive terraced crown, epitomizing the Art Deco style.

q: Name the architect behind these projects: Bank of Pennsylvania in Philadelphia; and contributions to the design of the U.S. Capitol in Washington, D.C.
n: Benjamin Henry Latrobe's notable works are the Bank of Pennsylvania in Philadelphia and contributions to the design of the U.S. Capitol in Washington, D.C.

q: Complete the statement: Paul Rudolph's architectural style is best described as ___.
n: Paul Rudolph's architectural style is Brutalism. Paul Rudolph is known for bold, complex designs contributing to the Brutalist movement.

q: Which architectural style is most closely tied to the work of Hector Guimard?
n: Hector Guimard's architectural style is Art Nouveau. Hector Guimard was a leading figure of Art Nouveau, famous for the sinuous Paris Métro entrances.

q: Which architect is credited with Lloyd's Building, London; Millennium Dome (now The O2), London; and Terminal 4, Madrid-Barajas Airport, Spain?
n: Richard Rogers's notable works are the Lloyd's Building in London, which features its services exposed on the exterior, the Millennium Dome (now The O2) in London, and Terminal 4 at Madrid-Barajas Airport in Spain.

s: Ludwig Mies van der Rohe — Notable Works
q: The following projects — Barcelona Pavilion, Spain; Farnsworth House, Illinois; Seagram Building, New York; and Crown Hall, Illinois Institute of Technology — are the work of which architect?
n: Ludwig Mies van der Rohe's notable works are the Barcelona Pavilion in Spain, the Farnsworth House in Illinois, the Seagram Building in New York, and Crown Hall at the Illinois Institute of Technology.

q: Combining engineering precision with architectural elegance in reinforced concrete, this Italian engineer-architect designed Rome's Palazzetto dello Sport and co-designed Milan's Pirelli Tower. Who was he?
n: An Italian engineer and architect renowned for his innovative use of reinforced concrete, combining engineering precision with architectural elegance, often through thin-shell structures and intricate geometries. Notable works: the Palazzetto dello Sport (Rome) and the Pirelli Tower (Milan, co-designed).

q: Founded in 1936 and credited with pushing modernist skyscraper design forward, this American firm produced the Lever House, the Willis Tower (once the Sears Tower), and led design of the Burj Khalifa. Name the firm.
n: An American architectural firm founded in 1936, renowned for its contributions to modernist architecture and skyscraper design. In 1952, partner Gordon Bunshaft pushed SOM's design of Lever House toward a new level of architectural recognition. Notable works: Lever House (New York), the Willis Tower (Chicago, once the world's tallest building), and the Burj Khalifa (Dubai, the tallest structure globally), with SOM as lead architect.

q: Which term best captures the architectural style practiced by Richard Rogers?
n: Richard Rogers's architectural style is High-tech Architecture. Richard Rogers pioneered the high-tech architecture movement emphasizing transparency and flexibility.

q: An American architect and theorist who championed 'complexity and contradiction' as a leading voice of postmodernism, and who designed the Vanna Venturi House and the Sainsbury Wing of London's National Gallery — who is he?
n: An American architect and theorist, a leading figure in the postmodern movement, advocating for complexity and contradiction in architecture. Notable works: the Vanna Venturi House (Philadelphia) and the Sainsbury Wing, National Gallery (London), which challenged strict modernist principles by referencing classical facades.

q: A key figure of the Vienna Secession and pioneer of modern Austrian architecture, this urban planner and architect designed the Karlsplatz Stadtbahn Station. Identify him.
n: An Austrian architect and urban planner, a key figure in the Vienna Secession movement and a pioneer of modern architecture in Austria. Notable work: the Karlsplatz Stadtbahn Station, exemplifying the transition from historicism to modernism.

q: Frank Gehry's body of work is most representative of which architectural style?
n: Frank Gehry's architectural style is Deconstructivism. Frank Gehry is a leading figure of Deconstructivism, known for unconventional, sculptural forms.

q: Whose body of work includes Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park, Japan; St. Mary's Cathedral, Tokyo; Tokyo Olympic Arenas (1964); and the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building?
n: Kenzo Tange's notable works are the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park, St. Mary's Cathedral in Tokyo, the Tokyo Olympic Arenas (1964), and the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building.

q: Known for a demanding, conceptual approach treating architecture almost as a linguistic system, this American architect and theorist designed the Wexner Center for the Arts and Berlin's Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe. Who is he?
n: An American architect and theorist known for a challenging, conceptual approach to design that treats architecture as a form of linguistics, famous for deconstructing the grid and creating spaces that challenge the user's perception of stability. Notable works: the Wexner Center for the Arts and the Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe, Berlin.

q: Paris Métro Entrances (early 1900s) all belong to the portfolio of which architect?
n: Hector Guimard's notable work is the Paris Métro Entrances (early 1900s) — iconic cast-iron designs with sinuous lines and floral motifs, many of which still adorn Parisian subway stations today.

q: In terms of style, how is I.M. Pei most accurately categorized?
n: I.M. Pei's architectural style is Modernism. I.M. Pei is celebrated for modernist designs with geometric forms and contextual sensitivity.

q: Identify the architect responsible for Helsinki Central Railway Station in Finland; and Cranbrook Educational Community in Michigan, USA.
n: Eliel Saarinen's notable works are the Helsinki Central Railway Station in Finland and the Cranbrook Educational Community in Michigan, USA.

q: Which architect's notable works include Guggenheim Museum Bilbao (1997); and Walt Disney Concert Hall (2003)?
n: Frank Gehry's notable works are the Guggenheim Museum Bilbao (1997), credited with revitalizing the city (the 'Bilbao Effect'), and the Walt Disney Concert Hall (2003) in Los Angeles, renowned for its acoustics and striking stainless-steel exterior.

q: Which architectural style is Sir Christopher Wren chiefly identified with?
n: Sir Christopher Wren's architectural style is English Baroque / Classical Architecture. Christopher Wren's work blends classical architecture with Baroque elements.

q: If asked to label Benjamin Henry Latrobe's architectural style in one term, which would you choose?
n: Benjamin Henry Latrobe's architectural style is Greek Revival. Benjamin Henry Latrobe introduced Greek Revival architecture to the United States.

q: These projects — Sagrada Família; Park Güell; and Casa Batlló and Casa Milà (La Pedrera) in Barcelona — were designed by whom?
n: Antoni Gaudí's notable works are Sagrada Família, Park Güell, and Casa Batlló and Casa Milà (La Pedrera) in Barcelona — all UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

q: Eugène Freyssinet is best known for working in which architectural style?
n: Eugène Freyssinet's architectural style is Structural Engineering (Prestressed Concrete). Eugène Freyssinet is celebrated as the father of prestressed concrete, a structural-engineering innovation.

q: Which of the following best names the architectural style of Richard Meier?
n: Richard Meier's architectural style is Modernism (New York Five). Richard Meier, of the 'New York Five,' is known for pristine white, geometric Modernist designs.

q: Founder of the Bauhaus School and a central figure of modernist architecture who pushed functional design and the merging of art, craft, and technology, this German architect designed the Bauhaus Building in Dessau. Name him.
n: A German architect and founder of the Bauhaus School, a key figure in modernist architecture who promoted functional design and the integration of art, craft, and technology. Notable works: the Bauhaus Building (Dessau) and the Gropius House (Massachusetts).

q: How is the architectural output of Frei Otto typically classified?
n: Frei Otto's architectural style is Lightweight/Tensile Structures. Frei Otto pioneered lightweight, tensile structural design achieving maximum efficiency with minimal materials.

q: Match the architect to this list of works: Yale Art and Architecture Building, New Haven; Milam Residence, Florida; and Burroughs Wellcome Headquarters, North Carolina.
n: Paul Rudolph's notable works are the Yale Art and Architecture Building in New Haven, a seminal example of Brutalist architecture, the Milam Residence in Florida, and the Burroughs Wellcome Headquarters in North Carolina.

q: Founder of Foster + Partners and known for sleek, sustainable high-tech design, this British architect reworked Berlin's Reichstag with a glass dome and designed London's 30 St Mary Axe, nicknamed 'The Gherkin.' Who is he?
n: A British architect and founder of Foster + Partners, renowned for sleek, high-tech designs and a pioneer of sustainable architecture. Notable works: the Reichstag renovation (Berlin) with its modern glass dome, and 30 St Mary Axe ('The Gherkin'), London.

q: A Bauhaus-trained Hungarian-American architect and furniture designer who helped popularize raw 'béton brut' concrete and cantilevered forms in housing, and who also designed the Whitney Museum building in New York — name him.
n: A Hungarian American architect and furniture designer (creator of the Wassily Chair), a Bauhaus protégé who popularized the use of monumental exposed concrete ('béton brut') and the cantilever in residential design. Notable work: the Whitney Museum of American Art building, New York.

q: How would Zaha Hadid's architectural style best be classified?
n: Zaha Hadid's architectural style is Parametricism / Deconstructivism. Zaha Hadid pioneered Parametricism and is closely associated with Deconstructivist form-making.

q: Proving Modernist ideas could thrive in the lush, humid setting of South and Southeast Asia, this architect — seen in Sri Lanka's Heritance Kandalama Hotel — earned the title 'Father of Tropical Modernism.' Who is he?
n: Widely revered as the 'Father of Tropical Modernism.' His work transformed the architectural landscape of South and Southeast Asia by adapting Modernist principles to the lush, humid, culturally rich context of the tropics. Notable work: the Heritance Kandalama Hotel, Dambulla, Sri Lanka.

q: Walter Gropius is most closely associated with which architectural style?
n: Walter Gropius's architectural style is Modernism (Bauhaus). Walter Gropius founded the Bauhaus School, a key institution of Modernist design.

q: A former dean of the Yale School of Architecture known for bold, complex Brutalist work, this American architect created the Yale Art and Architecture Building. Identify him.
n: An American architect and former dean of the Yale School of Architecture, known for bold, complex designs contributing to the Brutalist movement. Notable works: the Yale Art and Architecture Building (New Haven) and the Milam Residence (Florida).

q: Which of the following architects designed Steiner House in Vienna, Austria?
n: Adolf Loos's notable work is the Steiner House in Vienna, Austria, which exemplifies his minimalist aesthetic and rationalist design principles.

q: This British architect, recognized for modernist designs that boldly combined form, space, color, and materials, broke from academic convention with the Engineering Building at the University of Leicester. Who is he?
n: A British architect known for bold, modernist designs that combined complex forms and materials in innovative ways. Notable work: the Engineering Building at the University of Leicester (1963), recognized for its innovative use of space and materials.

q: Complete the statement: James Stirling's architectural style is best described as ___.
n: James Stirling's architectural style is Modernism (later Postmodernism). James Stirling was known for bold, modernist designs combining complex forms, colors, and materials.

q: A leading figure of the Arts and Crafts movement who valued craftsmanship and simple traditional forms, this English architect designed the Red House in Bexleyheath for William Morris. Name him.
n: An English architect and designer, a key figure in the Arts and Crafts movement, emphasizing craftsmanship and simple forms. Notable works: the Red House (Bexleyheath), designed for William Morris, and Standen House (West Sussex).

q: Weaving natural materials and organic form through architecture, furniture, and glassware alike, this Finnish designer — behind the Säynätsalo Town Hall and Paimio Sanatorium — offered a humanistic counterpoint between rigid high modernism and postmodern disillusionment. Who is he?
n: A Finnish architect and designer known for a humanistic approach to modernism, integrating natural materials and organic forms into architecture, furniture, and glassware. A master of form and planning that relates a building to its users. Notable works: Säynätsalo Town Hall, Paimio Sanatorium, and Villa Mairea in Finland.

q: Which architectural style is most closely tied to the work of Kisho Kurokawa?
n: Kisho Kurokawa's architectural style is Metabolism. Kisho Kurokawa was a founding member of the Metabolist movement, emphasizing flexibility and organic growth.

q: An architect's portfolio includes Airship Hangars at Villeneuve-Orly Airport (1923); and the Plougastel Bridge (1930). Who designed these?
n: Eugène Freyssinet's notable works are the Airship Hangars at Villeneuve-Orly Airport (1923), showcasing the potential of thin-shell concrete structures, and the Plougastel Bridge (1930), which at completion was the largest reinforced-concrete bridge, with three spans of 187 meters each.

q: A founding member of the Metabolist movement noted for elegant, refined buildings blending Japanese sensibility with Western modernism — which Japanese architect is this?
n: A Japanese architect and founding member of the Metabolist movement, known for elegant, refined modernist designs that blend Japanese sensibility with Western modernism, earning him the Pritzker Architecture Prize.

q: Whose dynamically curved designs — the TWA Flight Center, Dulles International Airport, and the Gateway Arch in St. Louis — used fluid geometry to evoke movement and the optimistic spirit of the Space Age?
n: A Finnish American architect known for innovative, sculptural designs that pushed the boundaries of modern architecture. Notable works: the TWA Flight Center at JFK, Dulles International Airport, and the Gateway Arch in St. Louis, all featuring dynamic curves and fluid geometry.

q: Based in Vienna and author of the essay 'Ornament and Crime,' this Austrian architect and theorist held that stripping away needless ornament marked cultural progress, as shown in his spare Steiner House. Who is he?
n: An Austrian architect and theorist, a pioneer of modern architecture. Renowned for his essay 'Ornament and Crime,' advocating for the elimination of unnecessary ornamentation and emphasizing functionality and simplicity. Notable work: the Steiner House in Vienna, Austria.

q: Which term best captures the architectural style practiced by Peter Behrens?
n: Peter Behrens's architectural style is Modern Industrial Design (Proto-Modernism). Peter Behrens pioneered modern industrial design and corporate architectural identity, foreshadowing Modernism.

q: San Cataldo Cemetery in Modena, Italy — these are among the notable works of which architect?
n: Aldo Rossi's notable work is the San Cataldo Cemetery in Modena, Italy, which showcases his metaphysical approach to architecture.

q: Regarded as one of the foremost late-20th-century architects for his monumental, geometric use of natural light, this American designed the Salk Institute and the Kimbell Art Museum. Name him.
n: An American architect known for monumental, geometric designs characterized by his use of natural light. Considered one of the foremost architects of the late 20th century. Notable works: the Salk Institute for Biological Studies (California), the Kimbell Art Museum (Texas), the National Assembly Building (Bangladesh), and the Yale University Art Gallery (Connecticut).

q: Nicknamed the 'Father of Skyscrapers' and the 'Dean of American Architects,' this key Chicago School figure and mentor to Frank Lloyd Wright designed the Wainwright Building. Who is he?
n: An American architect often referred to as the 'Father of Skyscrapers' and the 'Dean of American Architects.' A key figure in the Chicago School and mentor to Frank Lloyd Wright. Notable works: the Wainwright Building (St. Louis), the Guaranty Building (Buffalo), and the Carson, Pirie, Scott and Company Building (Chicago).

q: Name the architect behind these projects: Hôtel Tassel, Brussels; Hôtel Solvay, Brussels; and Horta Museum, Brussels.
n: Victor Horta's notable works are the Hôtel Tassel in Brussels, considered the first true Art Nouveau building, the Hôtel Solvay in Brussels, and the Horta Museum in Brussels, his former residence and studio, now a museum.

q: Blending traditional Japanese design with modernism and shaping Japan's post-war reconstruction and planning (echoing Le Corbusier's influence), this architect designed the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park and the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building. Identify him.
n: A Japanese architect who fused traditional Japanese styles with modernism, playing a pivotal role in post-war reconstruction and urban planning in Japan, and mentoring a generation of Japanese architects. Notable works: Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park, St. Mary's Cathedral (Tokyo), the Tokyo Olympic Arenas (1964), and the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building.

q: A leading figure of the City Beautiful movement who pursued monumental civic grandeur, this American architect and planner designed the Flatiron Building and wrote the influential 1909 Plan of Chicago. Who is he?
n: An American architect and urban planner, a leading figure of the City Beautiful movement. Notable works: the Flatiron Building in New York City and the Plan of Chicago (1909), which laid the foundation for modern urban planning in the U.S.

q: Which architect is credited with Salk Institute for Biological Studies, California; Kimbell Art Museum, Texas; National Assembly Building, Bangladesh; and Yale University Art Gallery, Connecticut?
n: Louis Kahn's notable works are the Salk Institute for Biological Studies in California, the Kimbell Art Museum in Texas, the National Assembly Building in Bangladesh, and the Yale University Art Gallery in Connecticut.

s: Ludwig Mies van der Rohe — Architectural Style
q: Ludwig Mies van der Rohe's body of work is most representative of which architectural style?
n: Ludwig Mies van der Rohe's architectural style is Modernism (International Style / Minimalism). Mies van der Rohe was a pioneer of minimalist Modernist architecture and the International Style.

q: The following projects — Glass House, Connecticut; AT&T Building (now Sony Tower), New York; and Seagram Building, New York — are the work of which architect?
n: Philip Johnson's notable works are the Glass House in Connecticut, the AT&T Building (now Sony Tower) in New York, known for its Chippendale-style top, and the Seagram Building in New York, on which he collaborated with Mies van der Rohe.

q: In terms of style, how is Philip Johnson most accurately categorized?
n: Philip Johnson's architectural style is Modernism (International Style), later Postmodernism. Philip Johnson introduced Modernist International Style architecture to the U.S. and later embraced Postmodernism.

q: Which architectural style is Le Corbusier chiefly identified with?
n: Le Corbusier's architectural style is Modernism (International Style / Purism). Le Corbusier was a pioneer of Modernist, functionalist architecture and urban planning.

q: Whose body of work includes Portland Building, Oregon; Humana Building, Louisville, Kentucky; and Disney Headquarters, Burbank, California?
n: Michael Graves's notable works are the Portland Building in Oregon, the Humana Building in Louisville, Kentucky, and the Disney Headquarters in Burbank, California — which features playful elements like the Seven Dwarfs supporting the building's pediment.

q: Celebrated for sculptural, shell-like forms integrated with their surroundings, this Danish architect is best known for the Sydney Opera House. Name him.
n: A Danish architect renowned for designing the iconic Sydney Opera House, celebrated for its innovative use of sculptural forms and its integration with the surrounding environment.

q: A member of the 'New York Five' known for luminous, pristine white geometric museum designs such as the Getty Center in Los Angeles — identify this American architect.
n: An American architect associated with the 'New York Five,' known for contemporary designs, often museums, that emphasize light and geometric forms rendered in pristine white. Notable works: the Getty Center (Los Angeles) and the High Museum of Art (Atlanta).

q: Drawing on Palladio's influence, this 17th-century English architect broke from Gothic and Tudor tradition to bring pure classical architecture to Britain, designing the Banqueting House in Whitehall. Who is he?
n: An English architect who introduced classical architecture to Britain, influenced by the works of Palladio, marking a departure from traditional Gothic and Tudor architecture. Notable work: the Banqueting House, Whitehall, London (1619) — the first building in Britain designed in a pure classical style.

q: Wainwright Building, St. Louis; Guaranty Building, Buffalo; and Carson, Pirie, Scott and Company Building, Chicago all belong to the portfolio of which architect?
n: Louis Sullivan's notable works are the Wainwright Building in St. Louis, the Guaranty Building in Buffalo, and the Carson, Pirie, Scott and Company Building in Chicago.

q: Identify the architect responsible for Reichstag Renovation, Berlin; 30 St Mary Axe (The Gherkin), London; and Beijing Capital International Airport Terminal 3, China.
n: Norman Foster's notable works are the Reichstag Renovation in Berlin, 30 St Mary Axe (The Gherkin) in London, and Beijing Capital International Airport Terminal 3 in China.

q: Known for elegant, contextually sensitive modernist geometry, this Chinese-American architect designed the glass Louvre Pyramid in Paris and the sharply angled Bank of China Tower in Hong Kong. Name him.
n: A Chinese-American architect celebrated for modernist designs that often incorporate geometric forms and open spaces, known for their elegance and contextual sensitivity. Notable works: the Louvre Pyramid (1989) in Paris and the Bank of China Tower (1990) in Hong Kong.

q: Which architect's notable works include Getty Center, Los Angeles; Barcelona Museum of Contemporary Art, Spain; and High Museum of Art, Atlanta?
n: Richard Meier's notable works are the Getty Center in Los Angeles, a cultural complex with travertine-clad buildings, the Barcelona Museum of Contemporary Art in Spain, and the High Museum of Art in Atlanta.

q: If asked to label Philip Webb's architectural style in one term, which would you choose?
n: Philip Webb's architectural style is Arts and Crafts. Philip Webb was a key figure of the Arts and Crafts movement, emphasizing craftsmanship and traditional forms.

q: These projects — Wexner Center for the Arts, Ohio; Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe, Berlin; and City of Culture of Galicia, Spain — were designed by whom?
n: Peter Eisenman's notable works are the Wexner Center for the Arts in Ohio, featuring fragmented forms and grid-based design, the Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe in Berlin, and the City of Culture of Galicia in Spain.

q: Otto Wagner is best known for working in which architectural style?
n: Otto Wagner's architectural style is Vienna Secession / Early Modernism. Otto Wagner was a key figure of the Vienna Secession and a pioneer of modern architecture in Austria.

q: Which of the following best names the architectural style of Oscar Niemeyer?
n: Oscar Niemeyer's architectural style is Modernism (Brazilian Modernism). Oscar Niemeyer is celebrated for curvaceous, monumental Brazilian Modernist buildings.

q: How is the architectural output of Frank Lloyd Wright typically classified?
n: Frank Lloyd Wright's architectural style is Organic Architecture (Prairie Style). Frank Lloyd Wright championed Organic Architecture and developed the Prairie House concept.

q: How would Louis Kahn's architectural style best be classified?
n: Louis Kahn's architectural style is Modernism (Structuralism/Monumental Modernism). Louis Kahn's monumental, geometric designs using natural light reflect a Structuralist strand of Modernism.

q: Celebrated for merging advanced technology with aesthetics in high-tech, sustainable design, this Italian architect co-designed the Centre Pompidou with Richard Rogers and later created The Shard in London. Who is he?
n: An Italian architect celebrated for high-tech and sustainable designs that integrate advanced technology with aesthetics. He co-designed the Centre Pompidou with Richard Rogers. Notable work: The Shard, a looped, faceted skyscraper in London.

q: A pioneer of lightweight tensile structures who also devised a convertible roof of variable geometry, this German architect-engineer created the sweeping cable-net canopies of the Munich Olympic Stadium. Identify him.
n: A German architect and structural engineer, a pioneer of lightweight structures achieving maximum structural efficiency; he also developed a convertible roof with variable geometry. Notable work: the Munich Olympic Stadium (1972), known for its sweeping steel-cable canopies.

q: Jørn Utzon is most closely associated with which architectural style?
n: Jørn Utzon's architectural style is Modernism (Structural Expressionism). Jørn Utzon's Sydney Opera House exemplifies Structural Expressionism within Modernism.

q: Complete the statement: William Van Alen's architectural style is best described as ___.
n: William Van Alen's architectural style is Art Deco. William Van Alen's Chrysler Building epitomizes the Art Deco style.

q: Which architectural style is most closely tied to the work of Renzo Piano?
n: Renzo Piano's architectural style is High-tech Architecture. Renzo Piano is celebrated for high-tech, sustainable designs integrating technology with aesthetics.

q: Which term best captures the architectural style practiced by Charles Rennie Mackintosh?
o: Art Nouveau / Arts and Crafts (Glasgow Style)
n: Charles Rennie Mackintosh's architectural style is Art Nouveau / Arts and Crafts (Glasgow Style). Charles Rennie Mackintosh developed the 'Glasgow Style,' blending Art Nouveau and Arts and Crafts sensibilities.

q: Known for elegant simplicity and the fusion of decorative art into design, this Scottish figure of Art Nouveau and Arts and Crafts developed his own 'Glasgow Style' in the Glasgow School of Art and Hill House. Who is he?
n: A Scottish architect and designer, a prominent figure in the Arts and Crafts movement and Art Nouveau style. He believed a revival of the Scottish Baronial style, adapted to modern needs, suited Scotland's climate better than imported Greek and Roman forms. Notable works: Glasgow School of Art and Hill House.

q: Skidmore, Owings & Merrill (SOM)'s body of work is most representative of which architectural style?
n: Skidmore, Owings & Merrill (SOM)'s architectural style is Modernism (International Style). SOM is renowned for modernist, International Style skyscraper design.

q: Regarded as a pioneer of modern industrial design and corporate identity in architecture, this German designed the AEG Turbine Factory in Berlin. Name him.
n: A German architect and designer considered a pioneer of modern industrial design, who played a significant role in the development of corporate identity through architecture. Notable works: the AEG Turbine Factory (Berlin), the German Embassy (St. Petersburg), and the Mannesmann Headquarters (Düsseldorf).

q: Match the architect to this list of works: Engineering Building at the University of Leicester (1963).
n: James Stirling's notable work is the Engineering Building at the University of Leicester (1963), recognized for its innovative use of space and materials, marking a departure from traditional academic architecture.

q: In terms of style, how is Antoni Gaudí most accurately categorized?
n: Antoni Gaudí's architectural style is Art Nouveau (Catalan Modernisme). Antoni Gaudí is the figurehead of Catalan Modernisme, a regional branch of Art Nouveau known for organic, fantastical forms.

q: Which of the following architects designed Seattle Central Library, USA; CCTV Headquarters, Beijing; and Casa da Música, Porto?
n: Rem Koolhaas's notable works are the Seattle Central Library in the USA, a striking glass-and-steel structure, CCTV Headquarters in Beijing, a looped skyscraper challenging traditional forms, and Casa da Música in Porto.

q: An architect's portfolio includes Nakagin Capsule Tower, Tokyo; The National Art Center, Tokyo; Nagoya City Art Museum, Japan; and Kuala Lumpur International Airport, Malaysia. Who designed these?
n: Kisho Kurokawa's notable works are the Nakagin Capsule Tower and The National Art Center in Tokyo, the Nagoya City Art Museum in Japan, and Kuala Lumpur International Airport in Malaysia.

q: A founding Metabolist whose work stressed flexibility and organic growth, this Japanese architect designed the modular, capsule-based Nakagin Capsule Tower in Tokyo. Who is he?
n: A founding member of the Metabolist movement in architecture, whose designs emphasized flexibility and organic growth. Notable works: the Nakagin Capsule Tower and National Art Center in Tokyo, and Kuala Lumpur International Airport, Malaysia.

q: Vanna Venturi House, Philadelphia; Sainsbury Wing, National Gallery, London; and Seattle Art Museum, USA — these are among the notable works of which architect?
n: Robert Venturi's notable works are the Vanna Venturi House in Philadelphia, a seminal postmodern residence, the Sainsbury Wing of the National Gallery in London, and the Seattle Art Museum in the USA.

q: Instrumental in bringing modernist architecture to the U.S. before later turning to postmodernism, this American designed the Glass House in Connecticut and New York's AT&T Building with its Chippendale-style crown. Identify him.
n: An influential American architect, a key figure in introducing modernist architecture to the U.S. who later embraced postmodernism. Notable works: the Glass House (Connecticut), a minimalist residence with transparent walls; and the AT&T Building (now the Sony Building, New York), known for its Chippendale-style top and designed in collaboration with Mies van der Rohe on the Seagram Building.

q: Figurehead of Catalan Modernisme, this Spanish architect pioneered the catenary arch (modeled on an inverted hanging chain) to build self-supporting forms without flying buttresses, and developed the trencadís mosaic technique seen at the Sagrada Família and Park Güell. Who is he?
n: A Spanish Catalan architect and figurehead of Catalan Modernisme, blending Gothic and Art Nouveau elements with vibrant colors, organic shapes, and intricate details. He pioneered the catenary-arch model and the trencadís broken-mosaic technique. Notable works: Sagrada Família, Casa Batlló, Casa Milà (La Pedrera), and Park Güell in Barcelona — all UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

q: Which architectural style is Adolf Loos chiefly identified with?
n: Adolf Loos's architectural style is Modernism (Rationalism). Adolf Loos rejected ornament and championed functionality and simplicity, making him a pioneer of architectural Modernism/Rationalism.

q: If asked to label Peter Eisenman's architectural style in one term, which would you choose?
n: Peter Eisenman's architectural style is Deconstructivism. Peter Eisenman is known for a conceptual, Deconstructivist approach treating architecture as linguistics.

q: Aldo Rossi is best known for working in which architectural style?
n: Aldo Rossi's architectural style is Neo-Rationalism. Aldo Rossi is a key figure of Italian Neo-Rationalism, emphasizing historical continuity and 'collective memory' in urban form.

q: Which of the following best names the architectural style of Rem Koolhaas?
n: Rem Koolhaas's architectural style is Deconstructivism / Contemporary Architecture. Rem Koolhaas is known for unconventional designs and influential urbanist theory within Deconstructivist/contemporary practice.

q: Name the architect behind these projects: James R. Thompson Center (1985); and Terminal 1 at O'Hare International Airport (1987).
n: Helmut Jahn's notable works are the James R. Thompson Center (1985), a government building in Chicago with a distinctive glass-paneled, cylindrical atrium, and Terminal 1 at O'Hare International Airport (1987), noted for its futuristic design and efficient passenger flow.

q: How is the architectural output of Alvar Aalto typically classified?
n: Alvar Aalto's architectural style is Modernism (Humanist/Organic Modernism). Alvar Aalto is known for a humanistic, organic strand of Modernism that integrates natural materials and forms.

q: Working without historical precedent, this German pioneer of Expressionist architecture — who also helped shape the International Style — designed the Einstein Tower in Potsdam. Name him.
n: A German architect and a pioneer of Expressionist architecture who also contributed to the development of the International Style, using no historical precedents in his designs. Notable works: the Einstein Tower in Potsdam, Germany, and the Mossehaus in Berlin.

q: Believing in the promise of mass production for domestic life, this Swiss-French architect and planner designed Villa Savoye and the Unité d'Habitation. Who is he?
n: A Swiss-French architect and urban planner, a pioneer of modern functional architecture known for his belief in the possibilities of mass production applied to domestic living. Notable works: Villa Savoye (France), Unité d'Habitation (Marseille), Notre-Dame du Haut (Ronchamp), and his urban plan for Chandigarh, India.

q: How would Eliel Saarinen's architectural style best be classified?
n: Eliel Saarinen's architectural style is Art Nouveau / Nordic Romanticism (early), Modernism (later). Eliel Saarinen began in Art Nouveau/National Romanticism before influencing American Modernist design.

q: Which architect is credited with Louvre Pyramid (1989); and Bank of China Tower (1990)?
n: I.M. Pei's notable works are the Louvre Pyramid (1989) in Paris and the Bank of China Tower (1990) in Hong Kong, characterized by its sharp angles and triangular frameworks.

q: The following projects — Banqueting House (1619), Whitehall, London — are the work of which architect?
n: Inigo Jones's notable work is the Banqueting House (1619) in Whitehall, London — the first building in England designed in a pure classical style.

q: Santiago Calatrava is most closely associated with which architectural style?
n: Santiago Calatrava's architectural style is Structural Expressionism / Neo-Futurism. Santiago Calatrava is known for sculptural, dynamic structures inspired by natural forms — Structural Expressionism.

q: Whose body of work includes Robie House (1910); Fallingwater (1935); Taliesin West (1937); and the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum (1959)?
n: Frank Lloyd Wright's notable works are the Robie House (1910) at the University of Chicago campus, Fallingwater (1935), Taliesin West (1937) in Scottsdale, Arizona, and the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum (1959) in New York City.

q: Villa Savoye, France; Unité d'Habitation, Marseille; Notre-Dame du Haut, Ronchamp; and Chandigarh, India (urban planning and buildings) all belong to the portfolio of which architect?
n: Le Corbusier's notable works are Villa Savoye in France, Unité d'Habitation in Marseille, Notre-Dame du Haut in Ronchamp, and the urban planning and buildings of Chandigarh, India.

q: Complete the statement: Inigo Jones's architectural style is best described as ___.
n: Inigo Jones's architectural style is Classical Architecture (Palladianism). Inigo Jones introduced pure classical, Palladian-influenced architecture to Britain.

q: Which architectural style is most closely tied to the work of Pier Luigi Nervi?
n: Pier Luigi Nervi's architectural style is Structural Engineering / Modernism. Pier Luigi Nervi combined engineering precision with architectural elegance in reinforced concrete.

q: Known for folding classical elements into modern design with whimsy and color (and for a famous Alessi teakettle), this American postmodernist created the Portland Building in Oregon. Identify him.
n: An American architect and designer, a prominent figure in the postmodernist movement, known for integrating classical elements into modern design with a sense of whimsy and color, including the iconic Alessi teakettle. Notable work: the Portland Building, Oregon, a landmark of postmodern architecture.

q: Often dubbed the 'father of American architecture,' this English-born American brought Greek Revival design to the U.S. and contributed to the U.S. Capitol. Who is he?
n: An English-born American architect, often referred to as the 'father of American architecture.' He introduced Greek Revival architecture to the United States. Notable works: the Bank of Pennsylvania in Philadelphia and contributions to the design of the U.S. Capitol in Washington, D.C.

q: Which term best captures the architectural style practiced by Fumihiko Maki?
n: Fumihiko Maki's architectural style is Metabolism / Modernism. Fumihiko Maki, a founding Metabolist, is known for refined modernist designs blending Japanese and Western sensibility.

q: Geoffrey Bawa's body of work is most representative of which architectural style?
n: Geoffrey Bawa's architectural style is Tropical Modernism. Geoffrey Bawa is revered as the 'Father of Tropical Modernism,' adapting Modernist principles to tropical climates.

q: Identify the architect responsible for Heritance Kandalama Hotel, Dambulla, Sri Lanka.
n: Geoffrey Bawa's notable work is the Heritance Kandalama Hotel, Dambulla, Sri Lanka — considered one of his greatest masterpieces and an early pioneer of sustainable, eco-integrated hospitality design.

q: Using aerospace software to realize sculptural, unconventional forms, this Canadian-American deconstructivist created the titanium-clad Guggenheim Museum Bilbao — sparking what became known as the 'Bilbao Effect' — and the Walt Disney Concert Hall. Name him.
n: A Canadian American architect known for a deconstructivist style characterized by unconventional forms and innovative use of materials, often using aerospace design software to realize his sculptural designs. Notable works: the Guggenheim Museum Bilbao (1997), credited with revitalizing the city (the 'Bilbao Effect'), and the Walt Disney Concert Hall (2003) in Los Angeles.

q: Which architect's notable works include AEG Turbine Factory, Berlin; Mannesmann Building, Düsseldorf; and German Embassy, St. Petersburg?
n: Peter Behrens's notable works are the AEG Turbine Factory in Berlin, a landmark of industrial architecture, the Mannesmann Building in Düsseldorf, and the German Embassy in St. Petersburg.

q: These projects — Red House, Bexleyheath; Standen House, West Sussex; and 1 Palace Green, London — were designed by whom?
n: Philip Webb's notable works are the Red House in Bexleyheath, designed for William Morris as a seminal Arts and Crafts residence, Standen House in West Sussex, and 1 Palace Green in London.

q: In terms of style, how is Marcel Breuer most accurately categorized?
n: Marcel Breuer's architectural style is Brutalism (Bauhaus origins). Marcel Breuer, a Bauhaus protégé, popularized exposed 'béton brut' concrete central to Brutalism.

q: The first woman to win the Pritzker Architecture Prize (2004), this Iraqi-British architect pioneered Parametricism with partner Patrik Schumacher and designed Baku's fluid Heydar Aliyev Center, earning her the nickname 'Queen of the Curve.' Who is she?
n: An Iraqi British architect who fundamentally redefined the possibilities of form and space in the 21st century. Alongside her partner Patrik Schumacher, she pioneered Parametricism, and in 2004 became the first woman to win the Pritzker Architecture Prize. Nicknamed the 'Queen of the Curve.' Notable works: the Heydar Aliyev Center (Baku), the Vitra Fire Station (Germany), and the MAXXI Museum (Rome).

q: Which architectural style is Victor Horta chiefly identified with?
n: Victor Horta's architectural style is Art Nouveau. Victor Horta was a pioneer of the Art Nouveau movement, integrating architecture with decorative ironwork.

q: If asked to label Robert Venturi's architectural style in one term, which would you choose?
n: Robert Venturi's architectural style is Postmodernism. Robert Venturi was a leading theorist of Postmodernism, advocating 'complexity and contradiction.'

q: Author of L'Architettura della città and designer of Modena's San Cataldo Cemetery, this Italian architect-theorist advanced the concept of 'Collective Memory' in urban form. Identify him.
n: An influential Italian architect and theorist, celebrated for his work in architectural theory and urban design. His seminal book, L'Architettura della città, emphasizes historical continuity in urban planning. Notable work: the San Cataldo Cemetery, Modena, Italy. He is closely associated with the concept of 'Collective Memory.'

q: Match the architect to this list of works: Cathedral of Brasília, Brazil; National Congress of Brazil; Palácio da Alvorada (Presidential Palace), Brasília; and Museum of Contemporary Art, Niterói.
n: Oscar Niemeyer's notable works are the Cathedral of Brasília, the National Congress of Brazil, the Palácio da Alvorada (Presidential Palace) in Brasília, and the Museum of Contemporary Art in Niterói.

q: Founder of the Office for Metropolitan Architecture (OMA) and known for unconventional design plus influential urban theory, this Dutch architect created the CCTV Headquarters in Beijing and the Seattle Central Library. Who is he?
n: A Dutch architect and theorist known for unconventional designs that have influenced contemporary architecture through both practice and theory. He founded the Office for Metropolitan Architecture (OMA). Notable works: the CCTV Headquarters (Beijing) and the Seattle Central Library.

q: Which of the following architects designed World Trade Center (2013), New York City; and Museum Reinhard Ernst (2023), Wiesbaden, Germany?
n: Fumihiko Maki's notable works are the World Trade Center (2013), a minimalist skyscraper in New York City with a reflective glass facade, and the Museum Reinhard Ernst (2023) in Wiesbaden, Germany, showcasing his signature clean lines and harmonious proportions.

q: Drawing sculptural, dynamic forms from nature and human anatomy, this Spanish architect-engineer designed the City of Arts and Sciences in Valencia and the twisting Turning Torso in Malmö. Name him.
n: A Spanish architect and engineer known for sculptural, dynamic structures often inspired by natural forms and human anatomy. Notable works: the City of Arts and Sciences (Valencia) and the Turning Torso (Malmö), a twisting residential skyscraper.

q: An architect's portfolio includes Einstein Tower in Potsdam, Germany; and the Mossehaus in Berlin. Who designed these?
n: Erich Mendelsohn's notable works are the Einstein Tower in Potsdam, Germany, and the Mossehaus in Berlin, noted for their dynamic forms and innovative use of materials.

q: St. Paul's Cathedral, London; Royal Observatory, Greenwich; and numerous churches in London, including St. Mary-le-Bow and St. Bride's Church — these are among the notable works of which architect?
n: Sir Christopher Wren's notable works are St. Paul's Cathedral in London, a masterpiece with a prominent dome, the Royal Observatory in Greenwich, and numerous churches in London, including St. Mary-le-Bow and St. Bride's Church.

q: This English architect, astronomer, and mathematician rebuilt much of London after the Great Fire of 1666, blending classical form with Baroque flourish in St. Paul's Cathedral and numerous city churches. Who is he?
n: An English architect, astronomer, and mathematician, instrumental in rebuilding London after the Great Fire of 1666. His works are characterized by classical architecture infused with Baroque elements. Notable works: St. Paul's Cathedral and numerous London churches, including St. Mary-le-Bow and St. Bride's.

q: Name the architect behind these projects: Flatiron Building in New York City; and the Plan of Chicago (1909).
n: Daniel Burnham's notable works are the Flatiron Building in New York City and the Plan of Chicago (1909), which laid the foundation for modern urban planning in the U.S.

q: Nicknamed 'the poet of concrete' and 'the great king of curves' for the monumental, flowing modernist buildings that define Brasília, this Brazilian architect designed the Cathedral of Brasília and the National Congress of Brazil. Identify him.
n: A Brazilian architect celebrated for modernist buildings with curvaceous, monumental forms integral to the identity of Brasília, Brazil's capital; nicknamed 'the great king of curves' and 'the poet of concrete.' Notable works: the Cathedral of Brasília, the National Congress of Brazil, and the Palácio da Alvorada.

q: Which architect is credited with Munich Olympic Stadium (1972)?
n: Frei Otto's notable work is the Munich Olympic Stadium (1972), known for its sweeping canopies of acrylic glass stabilized by steel cables, mimicking the Alps' silhouettes.

q: Kenzo Tange is best known for working in which architectural style?
n: Kenzo Tange's architectural style is Metabolism / Modernism. Kenzo Tange fused traditional Japanese styles with Modernism and influenced the Metabolist movement.

q: Hailed as 'the father of prestressed concrete,' this French structural engineer designed the Plougastel Bridge (once the longest reinforced-concrete bridge, with three 187-meter spans) and pioneered thin-shell concrete airship hangars. Who is he?
n: A pioneering French structural engineer, celebrated as 'the father of prestressed concrete.' His innovations revolutionized the use of concrete, allowing for longer spans and more daring forms. Notable works: the Plougastel Bridge (1930) and the thin-shell concrete Airship Hangars (1923).

q: The following projects — World Trade Center Twin Towers, New York City; Rainier Tower, Seattle; and Lambert-St. Louis International Airport Terminal, Missouri — are the work of which architect?
n: Minoru Yamasaki's notable works are the World Trade Center Twin Towers in New York City, Rainier Tower in Seattle, and the Lambert-St. Louis International Airport Terminal in Missouri.

q: Whose body of work includes Säynätsalo Town Hall; Paimio Sanatorium; and Villa Mairea in Finland?
n: Alvar Aalto's notable works are Säynätsalo Town Hall, Paimio Sanatorium, and Villa Mairea in Finland — exemplary of his holistic design philosophy.

q: Which of the following best names the architectural style of Moshe Safdie?
n: Moshe Safdie's architectural style is Modernism (Humanistic Architecture). Moshe Safdie is celebrated for a humanistic approach to Modernism emphasizing community and livability.

q: How is the architectural output of Louis Sullivan typically classified?
n: Louis Sullivan's architectural style is Chicago School. Louis Sullivan, the 'Father of Skyscrapers,' was a key figure of the Chicago School.

q: Whitney Museum of American Art (now the Met Breuer), New York; UNESCO Headquarters, Paris; St. John's Abbey Church, Minnesota; and IBM Research Center, France all belong to the portfolio of which architect?
n: Marcel Breuer's notable works are the Whitney Museum of American Art (now the Met Breuer) in New York, the UNESCO Headquarters in Paris, St. John's Abbey Church in Minnesota, and the IBM Research Center in France.

q: A leading figure of Art Nouveau, this French architect and designer is remembered for the cast-iron Paris Métro entrances with their flowing lines and floral ornament. Name him.
n: A French architect and designer, a leading figure of the Art Nouveau movement whose curvilinear, ornamental style became synonymous with the movement. Notable work: the cast-iron Paris Métro Entrances (early 1900s), many of which still adorn Paris subway stations today.

q: Identify the architect responsible for Crystal Palace, London.
n: Joseph Paxton's notable work is the Crystal Palace, London, a pioneering example of prefabricated iron-and-glass architecture built for the Great Exhibition of 1851.

q: Which architect's notable works include TWA Flight Center at JFK Airport; Gateway Arch in St. Louis; and Dulles International Airport near Washington, D.C?
n: Eero Saarinen's notable works are the TWA Flight Center at JFK Airport, the Gateway Arch in St. Louis, and Dulles International Airport near Washington, D.C.

q: An English gardener, architect, and engineer, he designed the Crystal Palace for London's 1851 Great Exhibition, an early landmark of prefabricated iron-and-glass construction. Who is he?
n: An English gardener, architect, and engineer, best known for designing the Crystal Palace, a pioneering example of prefabricated iron-and-glass architecture, built for London's Great Exhibition of 1851.

q: A pioneer of Art Nouveau who fused architecture with decorative arts and ironwork, this Belgian designed the Hôtel Tassel in Brussels, held to be the first true Art Nouveau building. Identify him.
n: A Belgian architect and a pioneer of the Art Nouveau movement, noted for the integration of architecture with decorative arts, ironwork, and organic forms. Notable works: the Hôtel Tassel (considered the first true Art Nouveau building), the Hôtel Solvay, and the Horta Museum, Brussels.

q: How would Minoru Yamasaki's architectural style best be classified?
n: Minoru Yamasaki's architectural style is Modernism (New Formalism). Minoru Yamasaki's elegant modernist designs are associated with the New Formalism strand of Modernism.

q: Michael Graves is most closely associated with which architectural style?
n: Michael Graves's architectural style is Postmodernism. Michael Graves was a prominent figure of the Postmodernist movement, blending classical elements with whimsy.

q: These projects — Centre Georges Pompidou, Paris; The Shard, London; and Whitney Museum of American Art, New York — were designed by whom?
n: Renzo Piano's notable works are the Centre Georges Pompidou in Paris, known for its exposed structural elements, The Shard in London, and the Whitney Museum of American Art in New York.

q: Known for elegant modernist designs conveying serenity and harmony, this American architect of Japanese descent designed the original World Trade Center Twin Towers. Who is he?
n: An American architect of Japanese descent, known for elegant, modernist designs that often incorporated elements of serenity and harmony. Notable work: the original World Trade Center Twin Towers, New York City, once the tallest buildings in the world.

q: Match the architect to this list of works: Vitra Fire Station, Weil am Rhein, Germany; MAXXI Museum, Rome, Italy; Heydar Aliyev Center, Baku, Azerbaijan; and Guangzhou Opera House, Guangzhou, China.
n: Zaha Hadid's notable works are the Vitra Fire Station in Weil am Rhein, Germany, the MAXXI Museum in Rome, Italy, the Heydar Aliyev Center in Baku, Azerbaijan — perhaps her most iconic work, a study in seamlessness — and the Guangzhou Opera House in Guangzhou, China.

q: Complete the statement: Erich Mendelsohn's architectural style is best described as ___.
n: Erich Mendelsohn's architectural style is Expressionism (later International Style). Erich Mendelsohn pioneered Expressionist architecture, later contributing to the International Style.

q: Which of the following architects designed Turning Torso, Malmö; City of Arts and Sciences, Valencia; and World Trade Center Transportation Hub (Oculus), New York?
n: Santiago Calatrava's notable works are Turning Torso, a twisting skyscraper in Malmö, the City of Arts and Sciences in Valencia, and the World Trade Center Transportation Hub (Oculus) in New York, a transit station with a winged roof structure.

q: An architect's portfolio includes Willis Tower (formerly Sears Tower), Chicago; Burj Khalifa, Dubai; One World Trade Center, New York; and the Lever House. Who designed these?
n: Skidmore, Owings & Merrill (SOM)'s notable works are the Willis Tower (formerly Sears Tower) in Chicago, once the world's tallest building, the Burj Khalifa in Dubai, the tallest structure globally, One World Trade Center in New York, and the Lever House, pushed toward a new level of architectural recognition by Gordon Bunshaft in 1952.

q: Pirelli Tower, Milan; Palazzetto dello Sport, Rome; and UNESCO Headquarters, Paris (with Marcel Breuer and Bernard Zehrfuss) — these are among the notable works of which architect?
n: Pier Luigi Nervi's notable works are the Pirelli Tower in Milan, the Palazzetto dello Sport in Rome, and the UNESCO Headquarters in Paris, collaboratively designed with Marcel Breuer and Bernard Zehrfuss.

q: Name the architect behind these projects: Habitat '67, Montreal; Jewel Changi Airport, Singapore; and Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art, Arkansas.
n: Moshe Safdie's notable works are Habitat '67 in Montreal, a revolutionary housing complex that reimagined urban living, Jewel Changi Airport in Singapore, and the Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art in Arkansas.

q: Which architectural style is most closely tied to the work of Daniel Burnham?
n: Daniel Burnham's architectural style is City Beautiful Movement (Beaux-Arts). Daniel Burnham led the City Beautiful movement, promoting monumental, Beaux-Arts-inspired civic grandeur.

q: Famous for the phrase 'Less is more,' this German-American modernist designed the Barcelona Pavilion, the Farnsworth House, and the Seagram Building. Name him.
n: A German-American modernist architect and pioneer of minimalist architecture, known for his aphorism 'Less is more.' Notable works: the Barcelona Pavilion, the Farnsworth House, the Seagram Building, and Crown Hall at the Illinois Institute of Technology.

q: Which architect is credited with Glasgow School of Art; Hill House; and The Willow Tearooms in Scotland?
n: Charles Rennie Mackintosh's notable works are the Glasgow School of Art, Hill House, and The Willow Tearooms in Scotland, showcasing his distinctive design approach.

q: Known for bold high-tech and postmodern work, this German-American architect designed Chicago O'Hare's Terminal 1, celebrated for its futuristic look and glass-paneled cylindrical atrium. Who is he?
n: A German American architect known for high-tech and postmodern designs characterized by bold forms and advanced engineering. Notable work: Terminal 1 at O'Hare International Airport (1987), noted for its futuristic design, efficient passenger flow, and distinctive glass-paneled cylindrical atrium.

q: Which term best captures the architectural style practiced by Eero Saarinen?
n: Eero Saarinen's architectural style is Modernism (Structural Expressionism). Eero Saarinen's sculptural, curving forms exemplify a Structural Expressionist strand of Modernism.

q: Champion of 'organic architecture' across a 70-year career spanning more than 1,000 built structures, this American architect developed the flowing, open-plan Prairie House and designed Fallingwater, the Robie House, and the spiral Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum. Identify him.
n: An iconic American architect who championed 'organic architecture,' aiming to create structures in harmony with humanity and the environment. He developed the Prairie House concept of open, interpenetrating interior space. Notable works: Fallingwater, the Robie House, Taliesin West, and the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum in New York.

q: Celebrated for a humanistic approach centered on community and livability, this Israeli Canadian-American architect designed Montreal's modular Habitat '67 and Singapore's waterfall-crowned Marina Bay Sands. Who is he?
n: An Israeli Canadian-American architect celebrated for a humanistic approach to architecture that emphasizes community and livability. Notable works: Habitat '67, Montreal — a revolutionary housing complex that reimagined urban living — and Marina Bay Sands, Singapore.

q: The following projects — Sydney Opera House, Australia — are the work of which architect?
n: Jørn Utzon's notable work is the Sydney Opera House, Australia, celebrated for its innovative use of sculptural forms and integration with the surrounding environment.

q: Father of Eero Saarinen and recognized first for Art Nouveau work before shaping American modernism, this Finnish-American architect is known for the Cranbrook Educational Community in Michigan. Name him.
n: A Finnish American architect recognized for his contributions to Art Nouveau architecture and, later, his influence on modernist design in the United States. Notable work: the Cranbrook Educational Community in Michigan, USA.

q: Whose body of work includes Bauhaus Building, Dessau; Harvard Graduate Center, USA; and Gropius House, Massachusetts?
n: Walter Gropius's notable works are the Bauhaus Building in Dessau, an embodiment of Bauhaus principles, the Harvard Graduate Center in the USA, which introduced modernist architecture to the campus, and the Gropius House in Massachusetts, his family residence showcasing Bauhaus ideals.

q: Helmut Jahn's body of work is most representative of which architectural style?
n: Helmut Jahn's architectural style is High-tech Architecture / Postmodernism. Helmut Jahn blended high-tech and postmodern design with bold forms and advanced engineering.
